## Claim checks

row 1: `runAgent` never listens for the child's `error` event
command: rg -n 'on\("error"' src/batch/agent.ts
observed: no match; the only child listener is `child.on("close", …)` at `agent.ts:136`
verdict: true

row 2: spawn` emits `error` with `ENOENT` when `pi` is off `PATH
command: env PATH=/nonexistent <bun> -e 'import {runAgent} from "./src/batch/agent.ts"; …'
observed: stack `at spawn (node:child_process:721:35)` with `code: "ENOENT"`
verdict: true

row 3: no `close` ever follows, so the timeout is the only settle path
command: bun mimic of `runAgent` (no error listener), `timeoutMs:2000`
observed: `rejected: timeout`, `events: []` — `close` never fired
verdict: true (current code; once an error listener is added bun does emit `close:-2`, hence the double-settle guard)

row 4: today prints the spawn stack then `pi timed out after 500 ms`
command: runAgent` repro, `timeoutMs:500`, `PATH=/nonexistent
observed: `rejected: pi timed out after 500 ms` after the spawn stack
verdict: true

row 5: rejection waits the full timeout length
command: runAgent` repro, `timeoutMs:2000
observed: rejected after ms: 2009 | pi timed out after 2000 ms
verdict: true

row 6: batch turns this into reason code `timeout` and halts
command: rg -n 'timeout' src/batch`; read `ReasonCode` in `prepare.ts
observed: no `timeout` in the union; a `runAgent` throw is caught as `unverifiable`; the ticket loop continues
verdict: false

row 7: "not installed, not on PATH, not executable" all yield `ENOENT`
command: spawn("./README.md", …)` vs `spawn("./does-not-exist", …)
observed: non-executable → `EACCES`/`-13`; missing → `ENOENT`/`-2`
verdict: partial

## Need

Blamed mechanism: `runAgent` attaches no `error` listener, so a spawn failure (`ENOENT`) is never rejected on the `error` path; only the timeout timer settles the promise.

Path the incident takes: `prepare` → `deps.agent` = `runAgent` → `spawn("pi", …)` at `agent.ts:114` → no error listener (only `close` at `136`) → timer rejects at `agent.ts:133` with `pi timed out after …`. Reproduced end-to-end with `PATH=/nonexistent`.

Need holds. The "reason code `timeout`" wording is wrong (the batch surfaces `unverifiable`), but the wrong-diagnosis need is real: a missing binary is reported as a model timeout after the full timeout length.

## Fix

Exists: `close` handler rejects on non-zero exit (`agent.ts:136-150`); timer rejects on timeout (`128-134`). Missing: an `error` listener and a single-settlement guard; `ChildHandle` (`agent.ts:27-32`) has no `error` overload.

Surface: `src/batch/agent.ts` (`ChildHandle` + `runAgent`) and `test/unit/batch-agent.test.ts` (one new case). Reaches the mechanism: yes — an `error` handler rejects immediately with the binary name and `err.code`, and clearing the timer plus a settled flag stops the later `close` (code `-2` once a listener exists) from double-settling.

## Definition of Done

1. `src/batch/agent.ts` declares `on(event: "error", listener: (err: Error) => void)` on `ChildHandle`, and `runAgent` registers `child.on("error", …)` whose callback rejects with a message naming `pi` and the error's `code`. Proof: `rg -n '"error"' src/batch/agent.ts`; read the callback.
2. The error path clears the timeout timer and sets a single-settlement guard, so a `close` following an `error` cannot call `resolve`/`reject` a second time. Proof: `rg -n 'clearTimeout|settled' src/batch/agent.ts`; read `runAgent`.
3. `test/unit/batch-agent.test.ts` has a test where a fake child emits `"error"` with `ENOENT` and never `"close"`, asserting `runAgent` rejects with a message matching `/pi/` and `/ENOENT/`. Proof: read the test; `bun run test test/unit/batch-agent.test.ts`.
4. The spawn-failure rejection does not contain `timed out`; the test in 3 asserts `not.toMatch(/timed out/)`. Proof: read the test; run it.

Today each fails: no `on("error"` (`rg`), no settled flag (`rg`), no error-emit test (`rg '"error"' test/unit/batch-agent.test.ts` → no match), and the only rejection for a missing binary says `timed out`.

## Verdict

`inline` — one file plus one unit test, precisely specified, no adjacent surfaces.
